issues.summary: No authentication on WebUI backend - complete system exposure
issues.evidence: CORS(app, resources={r"/*": {"origins": "*"}}) allows any origin to access all 94 API endpoints including /api/bot/start, /api/emergency/kill-all, /api/config
issues.likelyImpact: Unauthorized trading, config modification, data exfiltration, complete system takeover by any network client. An attacker can start/stop bot, modify grid parameters, access API keys, execute emergency shutdowns.
issues.suggestedFix: Add Flask-HTTPAuth or JWT authentication middleware before all routes. Store credentials in environment variables. Example: @auth.login_required decorator on all /api/* routes. Restrict CORS to specific origins (e.g., localhost:3000).

issues.summary: Live API keys exposed in plaintext config file and served via API
issues.evidence: LIVE_DELTA_API_KEY and LIVE_DELTA_API_SECRET stored in secrets/api_keys.env, accessible via /api/config/all endpoint without redaction. Keys: p1QrZ62WGTNW4NN9lsRP1iqzskqSMP (live trading account)
issues.likelyImpact: Account drainage, unauthorized trades, credential theft. If secrets file is committed to git (check .gitignore), keys are permanently leaked in commit history. Network attacker can drain entire trading account.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Never serve secrets via API endpoints - filter keys containing API_KEY, API_SECRET, PASSWORD from /api/config response. 2) Ensure secrets/api_keys.env is in .gitignore. 3) Rotate compromised keys immediately on Delta Exchange. 4) Use environment variables only for production deployment.

issues.summary: Config drift: state.json vs grid_config.env mismatched grid parameters
issues.evidence: state.json has REFERENCE_LEVEL=115000, GRID_LOWER=110000, GRID_UPPER=130000 but grid_config.env has GRIDBOT_REF=111000, GRIDBOT_LOWER=109000, GRIDBOT_UPPER=130000. Drift: REF off by 4000 INR (~3.6%), LOWER off by 1000 INR (~0.9%)
issues.likelyImpact: Strategy operates on wrong grid parameters. First BUY order placement incorrect, TP/SL calculations off, position sizing errors. P&L unpredictability, risk limits breached. Last writer wins = race condition on every bot restart.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Decide canonical values (recommend grid_config.env as source of truth). 2) Update state.json to match grid_config.env. 3) Implement config sync check on bot startup (fail if drift >0.1%). 4) Deprecate duplicate keys (Phase 1: unify GRID_* and GRIDBOT_* to single namespace).

issues.summary: Duplicate config keys: GRID_* and GRIDBOT_* coexist causing ambiguity
issues.evidence: Both GRID_LOWER=110000 (line 936) and GRIDBOT_LOWER=109000 (line 66) exist. bot/run.py:206-211 adopts GRID_* → GRIDBOT_* if GRIDBOT_* missing, but WebUI reads GRID_*, bot reads GRIDBOT_*. No single source of truth.
issues.likelyImpact: Frontend-backend desynchronization. User sets GRIDBOT_LOWER=109000 in UI, sees GRID_LOWER=110000 displayed. Strategy runs with GRIDBOT_* values, UI shows GRID_* values. Confusion, incorrect manual interventions.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove GRID_* keys entirely from grid_config.env. Update WebUI ConfigPanel.js to read/write GRIDBOT_* keys only. Update reconciliation service to write GRIDBOT_* to state.json. Add migration script to convert old configs.

issues.summary: Subprocess deadlock: bot process Popen with stdout=PIPE without reader thread
issues.evidence: bot_process = subprocess.Popen([...], stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, ...) at line 998. If bot writes >64KB to stdout, pipe buffer fills and process blocks waiting for reader. No background thread reading stdout.
issues.likelyImpact: Bot freezes on first verbose log burst (e.g., reconciliation report, error stack trace). WebUI shows 'running' but bot is deadlocked. Requires manual kill -9. Guaranteed failure on production deploy with debug logging enabled.
issues.suggestedFix: Change stdout=PIPE to stdout=None (inherit parent stdout) or redirect to log file. Alternative: spawn background thread to consume stdout/stderr continuously. Pattern: subprocess.Popen([...], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=log_file)

issues.summary: PID file race condition: concurrent writes possible without exclusive lock
issues.evidence: PID files (.guardian.pid, .bot.pid) written without fcntl.flock(). Multiple WebUI instances or PM2 restart during manual start can write same PID file concurrently. No exclusive lock check before process spawn.
issues.likelyImpact: Duplicate bot processes running simultaneously. Double trading = position chaos, risk limit breaches. Two guardians monitoring same positions = duplicate emergency actions. Difficult to debug (processes interfere).
issues.suggestedFix: Use fcntl.flock(pid_file_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB) before writing PID. If lock fails, process already running. Raise error instead of starting duplicate. Release lock on process exit.

issues.summary: Synchronous JSON file reads on hot path block Flask thread
issues.evidence: /api/positions (line 1869) and /api/state (line 1856) read positions.json (50KB+) and state.json (1KB) synchronously. json.load(open(file)) blocks Flask thread during disk I/O (100ms+ on HDD, 10ms+ on SSD). No caching.
issues.likelyImpact: 10 concurrent clients polling /api/positions every 1s = 1s response time (queueing delay). UI becomes unresponsive, stale data displayed, order execution lag. Under load, backend falls behind, WebSocket drops.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Cache JSON in memory, refresh on file modify event using watchdog library. 2) Load files async in background thread. 3) Alternative: migrate to SQLite for indexed queries. Expected improvement: 100ms → 5ms (20x faster).

issues.summary: N+1 file reads for PNL history endpoint
issues.evidence: /api/pnl-history reads entire bot/reports/ directory, opens each pnl_history_*.csv file in loop. 30 days of history = 30 file opens. No pagination, all files read on every request.
issues.likelyImpact: 300ms+ latency for PNL history request. Disk I/O spike on every UI page load. Does not scale beyond 1 year of data (365 file opens = 3s response time).
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Consolidate daily CSV files into single database (SQLite or append-only CSV). 2) Add pagination (e.g., last 7 days by default). 3) Cache aggregated results. 4) Use glob pattern to filter files before opening.

issues.summary: Unbounded polling loop with no backoff on repeated failures
issues.evidence: while True: loop with fixed time.sleep(GRIDBOT_HB_SEC=15s). On exchange API failure, continues polling at same rate. No exponential backoff, no circuit breaker.
issues.likelyImpact: Exchange outage = bot hammers API every 15s for hours. Rate limit ban possible. Wastes resources, masks real issues (logs flooded with same error). No graceful degradation.
issues.suggestedFix: Implement exponential backoff: on consecutive errors, increase delay (15s → 30s → 60s → 120s max). Add circuit breaker: after 5 consecutive failures, enter degraded mode (stop placing orders, keep monitoring only). Reset on first success.

issues.summary: Non-atomic JSON writes risk file corruption on mid-write crash
issues.evidence: write_config_file() (lines 363-400) does open(file, 'w') + writelines(). If process crashes mid-write, file left in partial state. Bot fails to start on next run (JSON parse error).
issues.likelyImpact: Crash during config save = corrupted grid_config.env. Bot cannot start, requires manual file restoration from backup. Rare but catastrophic (production downtime).
issues.suggestedFix: Use atomic write pattern: write to tempfile, then os.replace(temp, target). Already implemented in bot/reconciliation_service.py:179-199 (_atomic_write_json). Extract to shared utility, use everywhere.

issues.summary: Missing file locking on shared state accessed by bot and WebUI
issues.evidence: positions_demo.json and state.json written by bot, read by WebUI, no cross-process file lock. Bot writes while WebUI reads = partial update visible (torn read).
issues.likelyImpact: WebUI displays stale/partial position data. User sees incorrect P&L, makes wrong decision. Rare race condition, hard to reproduce, manifests under high update frequency (fast grid trading).
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Use fcntl.flock() for read/write locks. 2) Migrate to SQLite with WAL mode (no locking issues). 3) Use message queue (Redis) for state sharing instead of files.

issues.summary: 176 bare except blocks swallow errors silently across 39 files
issues.evidence: grep 'except:' found 176 instances. Examples: bot/strategy/gbot.py, bot/reconciliation_service.py. Errors caught but not logged, root causes masked.
issues.likelyImpact: Silent failures make debugging impossible. Order placement fails without log entry, position drift occurs, reconciliation alarm triggers hours later. Support requests unsolvable without stack traces.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace all 'except:' with 'except Exception as e:' + 'log.exception("Context: ...")'. Add structured logging to capture error context (order ID, price, timestamp). Use error aggregation (existing Error Intelligence System).

issues.summary: No retry logic in Delta Exchange client despite code comment
issues.evidence: Comment at line 30 says 'If you want, add retries here (urllib3 Retry)' but not implemented. Single network blip = order placement failure, no retry.
issues.likelyImpact: Missed fills on transient network errors. Manual intervention required to recover position. Under exchange congestion (high volatility), failure rate spikes. Grid strategy breaks (missing rungs).
issues.suggestedFix: Add urllib3.util.retry.Retry with exponential backoff: retries=3, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429, 500, 502, 503, 504]. Alternative: use tenacity library for declarative retries: @retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3), wait=wait_exponential()).

issues.summary: 56 subprocess calls risk shell injection if user input not validated
issues.evidence: grep found 56 subprocess.run/Popen/check_output calls. Examples: webui/backend/app.py:145, 607, 631, 998. Some pass user input without validation (e.g., tmux session name).
issues.likelyImpact: If user input reaches subprocess args without sanitization, shell injection possible (e.g., tmux session name with '; rm -rf /'). Currently low risk (no evidence of direct user input to subprocess), but dangerous pattern.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Validate all inputs to subprocess calls (regex whitelist). 2) Avoid shell=True, use list args instead. 3) Prefer Python stdlib over shell commands (e.g., use pathlib instead of 'ls'). 4) Add static analysis (bandit) to CI pipeline.

issues.summary: Minimal test coverage: only 12 test files, no integration tests
issues.evidence: glob found 12 test_*.py files. tests/ directory has 5 files, root has 7 ad-hoc tests. No tests for critical paths: bot/strategy/gbot_clean.py, bot/api/delta_client.py, reconciliation service.
issues.likelyImpact: Refactors break silently, regression risk high. No confidence in code changes. Production bugs discovered by users instead of CI. Debugging time wasted on preventable issues.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Add smoke tests for critical paths (order placement, reconciliation). 2) Use pytest with fixtures for exchange API mocks. 3) Integration test: bot startup → place order → verify positions.json updated. 4) Target 60% coverage on business logic.

issues.summary: Hardcoded absolute paths prevent deployment to new environments
issues.evidence: cwd: '/Users/shailendrasinghrajawat/Documents/WorkingBot' hardcoded in PM2 config. Every deployment to new machine requires manual path update in 6 places (line 10, 41, 72, 99, 126, 148).
issues.likelyImpact: Deployment friction, error-prone manual edits, config drift between dev/staging/prod. Breaks on colleague's machine with different username.
issues.suggestedFix: Use __dirname for relative paths in ecosystem.config.js. Example: cwd: __dirname. Alternatively, use environment variable: cwd: process.env.GRIDBOT_ROOT || __dirname.

issues.summary: Frontend expects flat config dict, backend sends nested {key: {value, section}}
issues.evidence: /api/config endpoint (line 1343) returns parse_config_file() which produces {key: {value, section}} structure. Frontend likely expects flat {key: value}. Mapping needed in frontend.
issues.likelyImpact: UI must unwrap nested structure, adds complexity. Not breaking (frontend likely handles it), but inconsistent API design. Future refactors may break silently.
issues.suggestedFix: Add /api/config/flat endpoint that returns simplified structure. Keep /api/config for advanced use (section metadata for UI grouping). Update frontend to use /api/config/flat for simple reads.

issues.summary: /api/liquidation/status may return None fields without null handling docs
issues.evidence: /api/liquidation/status endpoint (line 3076) reads .guardian_health.json which may have None/null values for risk_level, margin_utilization if guardian not initialized. Frontend assumes values always present.
issues.likelyImpact: UI displays 'undefined' or crashes on null access. Intermittent issue (only during bot startup before guardian initializes). User sees broken UI for first 10 seconds.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Backend: provide default values for all fields (e.g., risk_level='unknown', margin_utilization=0). 2) Frontend: add null checks (risk_level || 'unknown'). 3) API docs: document nullable fields.

issues.summary: account_snapshot_inr() returns mock data instead of real account balance
issues.evidence: Function returns hardcoded balance_inr=999999999 with comment 'conservative defaults; replace with real endpoints'. Not using actual Delta Exchange balance API.
issues.likelyImpact: Risk guards (assert_can_trade) operate on fake data. Loss limits not enforced correctly. Guardian bot monitors fake balance. Low severity IF actual balance tracking implemented elsewhere, but unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Implement real Delta Exchange account balance endpoint. API: GET /v2/wallet/balances. Parse available_balance, margin_used. Update account_snapshot_inr() to return actual values. Add caching (TTL=10s) to reduce API calls.

issues.summary: CCXT rate limiting enabled but no retry logic or backoff configured
issues.evidence: ex = ccxt.delta({...enableRateLimit: True...}) enables CCXT's internal rate limiter. However, CCXT retries not configured (no 'timeout' or 'rateLimit' options set). Default behavior may not match Delta Exchange limits.
issues.likelyImpact: Under heavy load, CCXT rate limiter blocks synchronously (waits). No visibility into rate limit state. If Delta changes rate limits, bot may get banned. Low impact if usage well under limits.
issues.suggestedFix: Configure CCXT options: 'rateLimit': 100 (ms between requests), 'timeout': 15000. Add retry wrapper around ex.fetch_* calls using tenacity library. Log rate limit hits for monitoring.

issues.summary: Mode-specific file paths computed dynamically without clear error path
issues.evidence: get_mode_specific_file() (lines 274-287) tries to import get_current_mode(), defaults to 'demo' on failure. Silent fallback may mask config errors (bot thinks it's in demo mode, actually wants live).
issues.likelyImpact: Bot writes to demo files while user thinks they're in live mode. Reconciliation reads wrong files. Hard to debug (no error logged). Low severity due to multiple safeguards (TRADING_MODE env var).
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Log warning if mode detection fails. 2) Add /api/status endpoint that returns current mode, file paths for troubleshooting. 3) Remove try/except, let import failure propagate (fail fast).

issues.summary: Telegram credentials hardcoded in config file instead of secrets
issues.evidence: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=8125591626:AAFNnlNXAabI7FOwNWBMdsBkeuvt61JB01E and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=8170794676 in grid_config.env. Should be in secrets/api_keys.env like Delta API keys.
issues.likelyImpact: Telegram bot token accessible to anyone who can read grid_config.env. If config file shared (team member, support), token leaked. Attacker can send fake alerts, spam chat. Moderate risk.
issues.suggestedFix: Move TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID to secrets/api_keys.env. Update bot/utils/env_loader.py to load from secrets. Add to /api/config redaction filter (SEC-002 fix).

issues.summary: API endpoint payload schemas not documented (OpenAPI/Swagger missing)
issues.evidence: 94 API endpoints in webui/backend/app.py, no API documentation generated. Frontend devs must reverse-engineer payload structure from code. Examples: /api/positions, /api/config, /api/liquidation/status.
issues.likelyImpact: Frontend-backend integration errors, wasted development time, silent payload changes break UI. New developers cannot discover API surface. No API versioning strategy.
issues.suggestedFix: 1) Add Flask-RESTPlus or Flask-RESTX for auto-generated Swagger UI. 2) Annotate endpoints with @api.doc(), @api.expect(), @api.marshal(). 3) Generate OpenAPI spec, serve at /api/docs. 4) CI check: fail build if undocumented endpoint added.
